supports_tools: diffres_run_lgssm_particle_filter (supporting: PF value_and_grad with diffusion_resampling and multinomial_stopped)
lgssm_gradient_demo.execution_mode: native script (unmodified) + capture driver (runpy of the unmodified script) + replay driver

runtime_environment.device: CPU only (heavy.sh: JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu); GPU memory 0 MiB before/after

settings.changed_vs_upstream: --nsteps 128 -> 16 (smallest-settings rule); --nparticles left at default 8. Everything else hard-coded in the script and unchanged: PRNGKey(666), F=0.5, Q=1, H=1, R=1, m0=0, P0=1, theta=(0.2,0.2), nmcs=1000, diffusion a=-1, T=2, dsteps=128, integrator=euler, ode=True, jitter=1e-5, resampling_threshold=1.
settings.monte_carlo_loop: The hard-coded 1000-iteration loop (2 jitted value_and_grad PF calls per iteration) ran in full; no part of the script was skipped. ~54 s inside the heavy.sh scope for the native run.

attempts.what: native run of the unmodified script
capture driver, first try: NOT STARTED by heavy.sh (exit 75, MemAvailable=3090 MB < 1200+2000); not an execution attempt

data_and_seed_provenance.data: Synthetic. ys/xs are produced by diffres.tools.simulate_lgssm inside the script (line 97); no external data.
data_and_seed_provenance.mc_keys: jax.random.split(key, num=1000), shape (1000,2) uint32; keys[0] equals key_simulation (the script reuses it)
data_and_seed_provenance.evaluation_point: theta=(0.2,0.2): F_theta = 0.2*I, H_theta = 0.2*ones((dy,dx)); Q, R, m0, P0 kept at the true values (script lines 40-43)

kf_grad_wrt_full_matrices_at_theta.chain_rule: d/dtheta0 = sum(dF*I), d/dtheta1 = sum(dH*ones) reproduce grad_true bitwise

reference_results.diffusion_vs_stopped: At nsteps=16, nparticles=8 the diffusion-resampling PF gradient has lower RMSE w.r.t. the exact KF gradient than multinomial_stopped (0.749 vs 1.244 for theta0; 2.820 vs 5.427 for theta1), the qualitative point of the demo.

notebooks/lgssm_gradient_demo/data/refer.contents: float64/uint32 at full precision: key, key_simulation, keys(1000,2), semigroup, trans_cov, obs_op, obs_cov, m0, v0, xs(17,1), ys(17,1), params, loss_true, grad_true, losses_dp/grads_dp (diffusion, 1000 / 1000x2), losses_rein/grads_rein (multinomial_stopped), kf_theta_{mfs,vfs,nll,mps,vps}, rts_theta_{mss,vss}, kf_true_*, rts_true_*, kf_theta_nll_via_FH, kf_theta_dF, kf_theta_dH, plus scalar settings (nsteps, nparticles, a, T, dsteps, ts, integrator, ode, jitter, nmcs, p1, p2, sig, xi, v0_scalar, script_sha256). Note: 'rein' is the script's own name for multinomial_stopped.
repr()-precision scalars, xs/ys values, MC summaries

notebooks/lgssm_gradient_demo/capture_ru.role: runs the unmodified script via runpy.run_path (sys.argv = script --nsteps 16 --nparticles 8) and saves its globals; afterwards calls upstream kf/rts/value_and_grad once more to record full filter/smoother outputs and the dF/dH gradient. No algorithm re-implemented.

notebooks/lgssm_gradient_demo/replay.py.role: fresh-process replay: direct calls to jax.random, diffres.tools.simulate_lgssm, diffres.gaussian_filters.kf/rts on saved inputs; PF replay by executing the script's source text verbatim up to (excluding) 'nmcs = 1000' (102 lines, sha256 b9ebeb795e0d7e714a7dec4136adfd8db1533f519d8119d55c6d249de22afc63) and calling its jitted diffpf_diff/diffpf_stopped for all 1000 saved keys; compares native printed values too.

replay_comparison.tolerances: keys/simulation: exact; KF/RTS/gradients: rtol=atol=1e-12; PF: rtol=atol=1e-9; native 8-digit printout vs captured: rtol 1e-7, atol 1e-8 (print rounding)
replay_comparison.observed: All 35 numerical replays (keys, xs, ys, KF nll/grad, kf/rts outputs at theta and at true params, dF/dH, chain rule, all 1000x2 PF losses and gradients) were BITWISE equal on CPU with x64. The 5 non-bitwise checks are the native run's 8-digit printed arrays vs full-precision captured values (max abs diff 4.3e-9 = print rounding), which also shows the native run and the runpy capture produced the same numbers.

lgssm_gradient_demo.figures: not applicable: the script produces no plots (prints only)
findings_for_tool_builders: smc_feynman_kac's nll is offset from the KF nll by the parameter-independent constant -log(nparticles): nll0 = -logsumexp(log_g0) without subtracting log(s) (diffres/feynman_kac.py, after the m0 sampling). Here KF nll 34.8292 - log(8)=2.0794 -> 32.7498; MC mean PF nll 32.8418 (diffusion) / 32.8433 (stopped) is above it by ~0.09, consistent with Jensen bias. The gradient is unaffected. A PF tool reporting 'log-likelihood' should state this (or document the offset) rather than silently compare raw PF nll with KF nll.

The KF tool in matrix form reproduces the demo exactly: value_and_grad of kf(...)[2] w.r.t. (F,H) at F=0.2I, H=0.2*ones gives dF=-0.8709261160639918, dH=-5.527063010352865, equal bitwise to grad_true w.r.t. theta via the chain rule (1-D case).

For the simulate tool: ys from simulate_lgssm with key = jax.random.split(PRNGKey(666))[0] and nsteps=16 equal the saved ys exactly; simulate_lgssm internally splits that key three times (x0, y0, step noise), so a tool must pass the key through unchanged to match.
The script's PF uses ys[0] at time 0 (log_g0) and kf also updates on ys[0]; both treat ys as length nsteps+1.
limitations: Run at --nsteps 16 instead of the upstream default 128 (smallest-settings rule); the default-size reference values (128 steps) were not computed. Monte Carlo loop, particle count (8) and all other hard-coded settings are at upstream values.

No independent closed-form check of the KF here (that is covered by tests/test_filters.py::test_kf, executor filters_tests); the KF gradient is checked against itself on replay and against the chain-rule matrix form.
PF MC statistics are from 1000 keys at nsteps=16 only; they are reference values for this configuration, not convergence evidence.
